full_judgment:
2. Facts, in brief, are that, the opposite party No.1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 93 of 1996 on 2-9-96 in the court of the learned Assistant Judge, Sadar Gopalgonj praying for declaration that the election of the Gopalgonj District Bus Owners Association held on 29-8-96 electing defendants as office-bearers and members of the executive committee of the association and the declaration of the result itself of the said election are all illegal and void, etc. stating that the said election was not conducted in accordance with bye-law and the rules thereunder and that the requisite period for filing objection of the voter list was not allowed in the election schedule and that the president elect is 31 years of age, but according to bye-law of the organization in order to become a president at least 35 years of age is necessary and that symbols of the candidates were not properly distributed in accordance with the provision of the bye law. 

 3. The plaintiff after filing the suit submitted another application under Order 39 rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for temporary injunction against the defendants restraining them from discharging their functions as office bearers. 

 4. The prayer for temporary injunction was opposed by the defendants by filing a written objection stating, inter alia, that there was no irregularity or illegality in the election and that the president elect had the requisite age and that the remedy regarding the irregularity, if any, in the election lies not by filing a suit but the remedy lies elsewhere according to the bye-law and, as such, the application was liable to be rejected. The learned Assistant Judge heard the matter and by the judgment and order dated 29-10-96 passed an order of temporary injunction in favour of the plaintiff restraining the defendants as prayed for till disposal of the suit. 

 7. Mr. Syed Ziaul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-petitioners, has placed the judgment of the courts below and argued that in the application filed by the plaintiff for temporary injunction the plaintiff admitted that the defendants already took charge of office and, as such, the order of temporary injunction on the basis of it was illegal and the said order therefore ought to have been set aside by the lower appellate Court. Without setting aside the said illegal order of the trial Court, the lower appellate Court made a third case and in spite of there being no prayer from either side, the lower appellate Court suo motu appointed a receiver in the matter and thus committed error of law and facts and hence the said judgment is liable to be set aside. 

 8. Mr. S M Moonir, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff opposite party No.1, on the other hand, submits that the lower appellate Court while hearing temporary injunction matter found that as a result of temporary injunction, a gap occurred and, as such, to stop the gap the learned District Judge had no other alternative but to appoint a receiver for management and preservation of the property of the association. He further submits that the receiver appointed by the learned District Judge already took charge and has been managing the affairs and, as such, any order at this stage upsetting the position shall jeopardize the interest of the parties and moreover the association itself shall face colossal loss and that in such circumstances the District Judge did not commit any error of law or fact in passing the impugned order for appointment of a receiver. 

 10. It appears from the judgment passed by the trial Court that after hearing the parties the trial Court found that the plaintiff had a prima facie good case and that there were violations of the provision of bye-law of the association in conducting the election of its office-bearers. The lower appellate Court, in its turn on consideration of the materials, found that the court below rightly held that the election was apparently illegal and so passed an order of temporary injunction restraining the defendants from functioning as office-bearers of the association in question. 

 11. The legality or otherwise of the judgment of the courts below whether the plaintiff had a prima facie case in his favour or not is not an issue before me in disposing of this Rule and, as such, I refrain from making any comments regarding the same. The only point before me for decision is whether the impugned judgment of the learned District Judge directing appointment of the local Magistrate as receiver is liable to be interfered by this court. The receiver is appointed under the provision of Order 40 rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Order 40 rule 1 CPC runs as follows: 

 13. In consideration of the facts represented by the parties it appears that the plaintiff filed the suit with the allegation of irregularity in holding the election of the defendants as office-bearers. The defendants, on the other hand, seriously contested the said assertion of the plaintiff. It appears from the impugned judgment passed by the lower appellate Court and the affidavit-in-opposition filed on behalf of the opposite party No.1 that Mr. Sekandar Hyat Rezvi, Magistrate, Gopalgonj already took over all charges of the association in view of the judgment and order dated 30-11-96. It has been stated in paragraph 4 of the affidavit-in-opposition that after passing the order dated 30-11-96 the said Magistrate took over all charges and since then he is managing and maintaining the affairs of the association. Further, it appears from paragraph 6 of the said affidavit-in-opposition that hearing of the suit has started on 17-8-97 and the opposite party No.1 has already been examined as PW 1 and 14-9-97 is fixed for further hearing of the suit. There is no reply in opposition to this counter affidavit filed by the opposite party No.1. In fact, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-petitioners finds it difficult to refute or deny the aforesaid averment made in the affidavit in opposition. 

 14. The instant suit being a suit claiming office of the disputed association, there being order in favour of the plaintiff for temporary injunction passed by the trial Court, it appears that, in fact, there arose a gap in the working of the affairs of the association. As contended on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party, to fill up the gap and to manage the day-to-day affairs of the association the lower appellate Court felt it just and convenient to pass the impugned judgment and order directing appointment of a receiver and hence passed the same. The receiver being a local Magistrate is said to have already taken charge of the affairs of the association pursuant to the order of the learned District Judge on 30-11-96. In such circumstances any order by this court setting at naught the order of appointment of receiver at this stage, passed by the learned District Judge in his discretion, I hold, should not be made in the interest of justice. 

 15. There is another important aspect of the case. As stated earlier, the hearing of the suit already started on 17-8-97 including examination of the witnesses for the plaintiff. The learned Advocates appearing on behalf of both the parties before me unequivocally assured that none of the parties would do anything that may delay the disposal of the suit. It appears that the learned District Judge while passing the impugned judgment and order also directed to dispose of the suit as early as possible preferably within 2(two) months from the date of receipt of the record by the trial Court. Though an order appointing the receiver was made by the learned District Judge his anxiety for early disposal of the suit is reflected in the impugned judgment and order. The said anxiety is absolutely reasonable, in the facts and circumstances of the case, more so in view of the appointment of a receiver by him in the suit. Be that as it may, in view of the fact that hearing has already started, I am of the opinion, that it should be concluded with utmost expedition, the disposal of the suit itself will sort out the crux and, as such, I do not think that at this stage of the suit -which is on the verge of conclusion, the order appointing the receiver should be disturbed. Tile learned Advocates of both the parties, in fact, candidly endorsed the view that early disposal of the suit itself shall lead to the solution of the problem involved.
